sources.title: Solid Waste Management Bye-Laws, 2020
sources.content: Section 4.1: Duties of the Municipal Corporation. The corporation is responsible for daily collection of wet waste and dry waste from all households. Household waste must be segregated. The local health inspectors and garbage collectors must ensure waste is cleared daily from public streets and bins.

sources.title: Public Lighting Infrastructure Guidelines
sources.content: Section 12.3: Maintenance of Public Lamps. The municipal authority shall maintain all public streetlights in working condition. Citizens can report broken or non-functioning streetlights, and the engineering department must repair or replace the bulbs within 48 to 72 hours of the complaint log.

sources.title: Road Maintenance and Pothole Repair Protocol
sources.content: Section 8.5: Road Safety and Pothole Rectification. The PWD or local municipal body is responsible for fixing potholes on public roads. Major potholes posing traffic hazards must be barricaded immediately and filled with cold mix or hot mix asphalt within 7 days of identification.

sources.title: Sewerage and Drainage Regulation Code
sources.authority: Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB)
sources.content: Section 17: Overflow and Blockage Clearance. BWSSB is mandated to maintain underground sewerage systems. Any overflow of sewage or blockage in public manholes must be cleared by sewage cleaning machinery within 24 hours of notification to prevent public health hazards.

sources.title: Water Supply Distribution Standards
sources.authority: Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB)
sources.content: Section 9: Safe Drinking Water Distribution. BWSSB is responsible for supplying potable drinking water to municipal wards. Water line leakages or contaminated water complaints must be inspected by ward water engineers and repaired to restore clean supply within 48 hours.

sources.title: Environmental Protection Bye-Laws on Waste Dumping
sources.content: Section 22: Prohibition of Dumping in Public Areas. Dumping of construction debris, plastic waste, or commercial garbage in vacant sites, water bodies, or roadsides is strictly prohibited. Offenders are liable for spot fines, and the local authority must clear illegal dumps.

sources.title: Right to Information Rules, 2005
sources.authority: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions
sources.content: Section 6(1): Request for obtaining information. Any citizen of India can file an RTI application seeking details or inspection of government records. The Public Information Officer must provide the information within 30 days of receiving the request.

sources.title: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016
sources.authority: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Govt of India
sources.content: Rule 15: Duties of Local Authorities. Every local authority shall be responsible for daily collection, segregation, storage, transportation, processing, and disposal of municipal solid waste. Central rules mandate door-to-door collection of segregated waste and prohibition of littering in all cities of India.

sources.title: National Street Light National Programme (SLNP) Guidelines
sources.authority: Ministry of Power, Govt of India
sources.content: Section 2.4: Maintenance of Smart Lighting. Local municipal bodies under the SLNP must ensure that all public lamps and streetlights are functional. Maintenance agencies are obligated to repair or replace non-functional streetlights within 72 hours of citizen reports.

sources.title: Indian Road Congress (IRC) Maintenance Standards
sources.authority: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Govt of India
sources.content: IRC Section 5: Maintenance Operations. Pothole repair and asphalt patching must be executed on all municipal and public roads within a maximum of 7 to 10 days of defect identification to ensure commuter safety and prevent traffic bottlenecks.

sources.title: National Sewerage and Urban Drainage Guidelines
sources.authority: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Govt of India
sources.content: Section 14: Sewer Pipeline Rectification. Municipal sanitation units must clear blocked pipelines and sewage overflows from residential streets within 24 to 48 hours to minimize bacterial hazards and protect public health.

sources.title: National Water Quality Standards & Distribution Guidelines
sources.authority: Ministry of Jal Shakti, Govt of India
sources.content: Rule 8: Quality Assurance of Water Supply. Supply of clean drinking water is a core municipal function. Complaints regarding contaminated water or major pipeline leakages must be attended to immediately and resolved within 48 hours.
